commit_message:
[WebGPU] Preserve Wasm host pointer widths (#25075)

I hit this while running JAX → IREE → WebGPU inside JupyterLite with
wasm64.

The WebGPU bridge passes host pointers as uint32_t and reads pointer
tables assuming four-byte entries. This truncates wasm64 addresses and
misreads multi-block instruction streams.

Use uintptr_t for host pointers and handle their width in JavaScript.
GPU handles and instruction words remain 32-bit. This also handles
signed wasm32 pointers above 2 GiB correctly.
Validates this for wasm32/wasm64.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: samples

commit_message:
[Bazel] Fix bitcode library include roots when IREE is an external repo

The fixed "-I runtime/src", "-I ." and llvm-project header paths just work if IREE is the main bazel module.
For IREE as a dependency embedded in another bazel module, those need to use the canonical repo names ("external/" + <repo-name>).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Lower RISC-V V f16 vfmacc, vfwmacc, and Zvfhmin inner_tiled MMA. (#25000)

Lowers the RISC-V V f16 `inner_tiled` MMA paths. Native f16 enums are
already on main from #24858. This adds lowering, the widening
`vfwmacc.vf` pair, and the `+zvfhmin`-only fallbacks. All of them reuse
`lowerRiscvVFmaccLike` and the hoisted accumulator legalization from
#24933. Tile N is `vlen/8`.

| Encoding | `+zvfh` | `+zvfhmin` only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| f16×f16→f16 | `llvm.riscv.vfmacc` (`MMA_RISCV_V_VFMACC_*_F16_F16`) |
`extf` the accumulator to f32, f32 `vfmacc`, `truncf` back
(`*_F16_F16_WIDENF32`) |
| f16×f16→f32 | `llvm.riscv.vfwmacc` (`MMA_RISCV_V_VFWMACC_*_F32_F16`) |
`extf` both panels, then f32 `vfmacc` (`*_F32_F16_CASTF32`) |

`+zvfh` implies `+zvfhmin`. When both are legal, the earlier enum wins:
native `vfmacc` for an f16 accumulator, `vfwmacc` for an f32
accumulator. At VLEN=256 the cost model picks `intrinsics_m` 14
(native), 7 (`vfwmacc`), and 6 (both `+zvfhmin` paths). CASTF32 and
WIDENF32 bill the widened f32 vector operand as f32.

Performance is tracked on #24932. On the X60 (VLEN=256), 1-thread
inner_tiled is faster than the mmt4d ukernel for native f16 and
`vfwmacc`. The 4-thread and 8-thread large shapes are still slower.
Native f16 is non-widening `vfmacc`; the f16 ukernel widens with
`vfwmacc`, so that ratio is not the same instruction sequence. `vfwmacc`
is the closer comparison.

Assisted-by: Cursor

Towards #24311

---------

Signed-off-by: Terence <terrencemahlatini@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Stream] Avoid repeated transfers for concrete await results

Usage refinement repeatedly inserted transfers after an await whose
concrete result lifetime differed from the inferred lifetime. Each
rewrite requeued the await, so the pass never finished.

Skip the transition when the result's only use is a transfer to a concrete
lifetime, matching the existing streamable-op overload. Also correct that
overload's comment to describe this check; its behavior is unchanged.

Add tests for a variable parameter load followed by an await and for an
await result with an existing transfer.

Fixes #25048

Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>
Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[WebGPU] Preserve Wasm host pointer widths (#25075)

I hit this while running JAX → IREE → WebGPU inside JupyterLite with
wasm64.

The WebGPU bridge passes host pointers as uint32_t and reads pointer
tables assuming four-byte entries. This truncates wasm64 addresses and
misreads multi-block instruction streams.

Use uintptr_t for host pointers and handle their width in JavaScript.
GPU handles and instruction words remain 32-bit. This also handles
signed wasm32 pointers above 2 GiB correctly.
Validates this for wasm32/wasm64.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: setup_metadata

commit_message:
[WebGPU] Preserve Wasm host pointer widths (#25075)

I hit this while running JAX → IREE → WebGPU inside JupyterLite with
wasm64.

The WebGPU bridge passes host pointers as uint32_t and reads pointer
tables assuming four-byte entries. This truncates wasm64 addresses and
misreads multi-block instruction streams.

Use uintptr_t for host pointers and handle their width in JavaScript.
GPU handles and instruction words remain 32-bit. This also handles
signed wasm32 pointers above 2 GiB correctly.
Validates this for wasm32/wasm64.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert torchao affine quantization to LinalgExt

Extends `ConvertTorchQuantizationToLinalgExt` to
`torchao.quantize_affine` and `torchao.dequantize_affine`, using their
`block_size` as the block size of the PT2E operand checks and builders.
A non-constant `block_size` entry, which `torch.export` gives for
per-tensor blocks of dynamic dimensions, spans its dimension and is
checked at runtime, as in the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

Besides the cases the PT2E ops decline, torchao ops with float zero
points, scales narrower than the real values, non-integral bounds,
non-constant `block_size` entries for static dimensions, or blocks that
split a dynamic dimension are left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.
Ops with non-constant bounds, float8 storage, or scales and zero points
laid out unlike the blocks are not converted either; Torch-to-Linalg
does not support them.

Depends on llvm/torch-mlir#4843 and a torch-mlir integrate.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

`torchao.quantize_affine` and `torchao.dequantize_affine`, using their

A non-constant `block_size` entry, which `torch.export` gives for
per-tensor blocks of dynamic dimensions, spans its dimension and is
checked at runtime, as in the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

points, scales narrower than the real values, non-integral bounds,
non-constant `block_size` entries for static dimensions, or blocks that
split a dynamic dimension are left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

laid out unlike the blocks are not converted either; Torch-to-Linalg
does not support them.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert torchao affine quantization to LinalgExt

Extends `ConvertTorchQuantizationToLinalgExt` to
`torchao.quantize_affine` and `torchao.dequantize_affine`, using their
`block_size` as the block size of the PT2E operand checks and builders.
A non-constant `block_size` entry, which `torch.export` gives for
per-tensor blocks of dynamic dimensions, spans its dimension and is
checked at runtime, as in the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

Besides the cases the PT2E ops decline, torchao ops with float zero
points, scales narrower than the real values, non-integral bounds,
non-constant `block_size` entries for static dimensions, or blocks that
split a dynamic dimension are left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.
Ops with non-constant bounds, float8 storage, or scales and zero points
laid out unlike the blocks are not converted either; Torch-to-Linalg
does not support them.

Depends on llvm/torch-mlir#4843 and a torch-mlir integrate.

Part of #24862.

commit_message:
[Bazel] Fix flatcc and bitcode library include paths when IREE is an external repo (#25101)

The fixed paths ("-I runtime/src", "-I .", fixed llvm-project header
paths) just work if IREE is the main bazel module. For IREE as a
dependency embedded in another bazel module, the paths need to be
prefixed with "external/" + repo-name with repo-name being the canonical
repo-name used by the main bazel module.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Lower RISC-V V f16 vfmacc, vfwmacc, and Zvfhmin inner_tiled MMA. (#25000)

Lowers the RISC-V V f16 `inner_tiled` MMA paths. Native f16 enums are
already on main from #24858. This adds lowering, the widening
`vfwmacc.vf` pair, and the `+zvfhmin`-only fallbacks. All of them reuse
`lowerRiscvVFmaccLike` and the hoisted accumulator legalization from
#24933. Tile N is `vlen/8`.

| Encoding | `+zvfh` | `+zvfhmin` only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| f16×f16→f16 | `llvm.riscv.vfmacc` (`MMA_RISCV_V_VFMACC_*_F16_F16`) |
`extf` the accumulator to f32, f32 `vfmacc`, `truncf` back
(`*_F16_F16_WIDENF32`) |
| f16×f16→f32 | `llvm.riscv.vfwmacc` (`MMA_RISCV_V_VFWMACC_*_F32_F16`) |
`extf` both panels, then f32 `vfmacc` (`*_F32_F16_CASTF32`) |

`+zvfh` implies `+zvfhmin`. When both are legal, the earlier enum wins:
native `vfmacc` for an f16 accumulator, `vfwmacc` for an f32
accumulator. At VLEN=256 the cost model picks `intrinsics_m` 14
(native), 7 (`vfwmacc`), and 6 (both `+zvfhmin` paths). CASTF32 and
WIDENF32 bill the widened f32 vector operand as f32.

Performance is tracked on #24932. On the X60 (VLEN=256), 1-thread
inner_tiled is faster than the mmt4d ukernel for native f16 and
`vfwmacc`. The 4-thread and 8-thread large shapes are still slower.
Native f16 is non-widening `vfmacc`; the f16 ukernel widens with
`vfwmacc`, so that ratio is not the same instruction sequence. `vfwmacc`
is the closer comparison.

Assisted-by: Cursor

Towards #24311

commit_message:
[CodeGen] Fix linkExecutables creating dangling references

linkExecutablesInto renames every root reference to a source executable (hal.executable.lookup … executable(@src)) to the linked executable. It did not chech that all of @src's variants were moved, but only considered the current target being linked.

An executable can have variants for more than one target. Each backend links its own variants in a separate call. E.g. the same dispatch placed on a CPU device and a VMVX device.

Without the fix, lookups for the remaining variants are renamed to a linked executable that doesn't contain their variant/is backend specific. The function refs nameing the fully-qualified-variant explicitly stays correct, but the lookup and its function disagree. At runtime this fails when the module loads ("device does not support any variant of executable …"), or a function is looked up in the wrong executable.

The vmvx lit-test  reproduces this: the vmvx case's lookup ends up on the CPU-only @link_executables_linked.

Fix: if only some of an executable's variants were linked, don't rename its root refs globally. Instead, point each lookup at whichever executable its function lookups name.

Co-Authored-by: Claude

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[CodeGen] Fix linkExecutables creating dangling references

linkExecutablesInto renames every root reference to a source executable (hal.executable.lookup … executable(@src)) to the linked executable. It did not chech that all of @src's variants were moved, but only considered the current target being linked.

An executable can have variants for more than one target. Each backend links its own variants in a separate call. E.g. the same dispatch placed on a CPU device and a VMVX device.

Without the fix, lookups for the remaining variants are renamed to a linked executable that doesn't contain their variant/is backend specific. The function refs nameing the fully-qualified-variant explicitly stays correct, but the lookup and its function disagree. At runtime this fails when the module loads ("device does not support any variant of executable …"), or a function is looked up in the wrong executable.

The vmvx lit-test  reproduces this: the vmvx case's lookup ends up on the CPU-only @link_executables_linked.

Fix: if only some of an executable's variants were linked, don't rename its root refs globally. Instead, point each lookup at whichever executable its function lookups name.

Co-Authored-by: Claude

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: Unit Test / Linux (x86_64)

Without the fix, lookups for the remaining variants are renamed to a linked executable that doesn't contain their variant/is backend specific. commit_message:
[CodeGen] Fix linkExecutables creating dangling references

linkExecutablesInto renames every root reference to a source executable (hal.executable.lookup … executable(@src)) to the linked executable. It did not chech that all of @src's variants were moved, but only considered the current target being linked.

An executable can have variants for more than one target. Each backend links its own variants in a separate call. E.g. the same dispatch placed on a CPU device and a VMVX device.

Without the fix, lookups for the remaining variants are renamed to a linked executable that doesn't contain their variant/is backend specific. The function refs nameing the fully-qualified-variant explicitly stays correct, but the lookup and its function disagree. At runtime this fails when the module loads ("device does not support any variant of executable …"), or a function is looked up in the wrong executable.

The vmvx lit-test  reproduces this: the vmvx case's lookup ends up on the CPU-only @link_executables_linked.

Fix: if only some of an executable's variants were linked, don't rename its root refs globally. Instead, point each lookup at whichever executable its function lookups name.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Lower RISC-V V f16 vfmacc, vfwmacc, and Zvfhmin inner_tiled MMA. (#25000)

Lowers the RISC-V V f16 `inner_tiled` MMA paths. Native f16 enums are
already on main from #24858. This adds lowering, the widening
`vfwmacc.vf` pair, and the `+zvfhmin`-only fallbacks. All of them reuse
`lowerRiscvVFmaccLike` and the hoisted accumulator legalization from
#24933. Tile N is `vlen/8`.

| Encoding | `+zvfh` | `+zvfhmin` only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| f16×f16→f16 | `llvm.riscv.vfmacc` (`MMA_RISCV_V_VFMACC_*_F16_F16`) |
`extf` the accumulator to f32, f32 `vfmacc`, `truncf` back
(`*_F16_F16_WIDENF32`) |
| f16×f16→f32 | `llvm.riscv.vfwmacc` (`MMA_RISCV_V_VFWMACC_*_F32_F16`) |
`extf` both panels, then f32 `vfmacc` (`*_F32_F16_CASTF32`) |

`+zvfh` implies `+zvfhmin`. When both are legal, the earlier enum wins:
native `vfmacc` for an f16 accumulator, `vfwmacc` for an f32
accumulator. At VLEN=256 the cost model picks `intrinsics_m` 14
(native), 7 (`vfwmacc`), and 6 (both `+zvfhmin` paths). CASTF32 and
WIDENF32 bill the widened f32 vector operand as f32.

Performance is tracked on #24932. On the X60 (VLEN=256), 1-thread
inner_tiled is faster than the mmt4d ukernel for native f16 and
`vfwmacc`. The 4-thread and 8-thread large shapes are still slower.
Native f16 is non-widening `vfmacc`; the f16 ukernel widens with
`vfwmacc`, so that ratio is not the same instruction sequence. `vfwmacc`
is the closer comparison.
